message:
Plain words: blind digging cannot feel a jam, so the digger must feel current and back itself out. I take from the CA2784416C - Systems, devices, and/or methods regarding excavating - Google Patents (E56) and the Systems, devices, and/or methods regarding excavating (E57) the finding that an excavator automatically controls crowd motion in response to an automatically detected stall condition at the hoist motor to avoid stalling the bucket in the bank, and the autonomous current-limited dig control maps that stall-avoidance to this robot by slowing the ladder feed on high motor current and reversing briefly on stall. Detection plus reverse takes 0.600 s from the fiducial final-align error budget and stall current backout timing simulation (E58) against heating over 300 s from the battery mixed duty runtime and motor heating estimate (E44); everyday scale says a blink against minutes to overheat, so the motor survives.

Plain words: coarse driving only gets the robot near the bin, the camera tag centres the pour. I take from the Advanced Edge Detection of AprilTags for Precise Docking Maneuvers of Mobile Robots (E54) the finding that dead reckoning still induces large errors but tag-guided docking reaches average deviation about 4.5 cm and 0.4 deg, and from the Indoor Hydroponics Robot System for Automated Seeding and Logistics (E55) the finding that AprilTag Visual Fiducial System, meaning printed square markers for camera pose, placed at every docking location minimises position offset, and the fiducial-guided auto-align dump maps that pad-relative docking to this robot by measuring pose to the bin tag then creeping into line before tilting. Pose error is 0.030 m to 0.040 m at 1.00 m to 2.00 m range and correcting 0.150 m at 0.100 m per s takes 1.50 s from the fiducial final-align error budget and stall current backout timing simulation (E58), inside 0.100 m to 0.150 m bounded drift from the blind localization drift growth odometry plus IMU without external fix simulation (E33); everyday scale says a shoe length trimmed to finger width, enough for a 0.150 m outlet over the bin mouth.

Plain words: Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead is right that a raised load can tip, so autonomy must refuse to dump on a slope. I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the Centre of Gravity (CG, meaning balance point of the machine), to mean from blind-operation view that the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU, meaning motion sensor for tilt and turn) tilt check must gate the tilt command and trips stay at 15.0 kg with 0.150 m lip clearance from the tip dump clearance deployed vs stowed and pressure check simulation (E51). Safety factor 1.69 on flat ground is like a loaded wheelbarrow held down, so dumping only when level keeps it upright.

Not ready, because camera and compute power in the mass sum with Power Structure and Integration Lead and the fiducial-visibility bench test are still open.
